overview.name: EcoGiro
overview.tagline: Your recycling, their opportunity, our future.
overview.summary: EcoGiro is a two-month UX/UI product design project developed by a five-person team. The mobile-first experience connects plastic identification and preparation with collection requests, recycler responses through Telegram, and eco-points after a completed handoff.

metadata.label: My contribution
metadata.value: Research framing, insight synthesis, user flows, information architecture, contextual education, and pitch narrative.

benefit.title: Recycle with confidence
benefit.description: The experience turns uncertainty about plastic into a clear next step: identify it, prepare it, and request a convenient handoff. It connects citizen convenience with the information recyclers need and the material traceability collection centers seek.

items.title: Citizens
items.description: Understand what to do with each material and choose where and when to request collection.

items.title: Recyclers
items.description: Know the material, estimated quantity, condition, address, and proposed time before deciding whether to collect.

items.title: Collection centers
items.description: Connect incoming material with a traceable record and a future service for operational coordination.

problem.title: Good intentions need a connection
paragraphs: The research described a fragmented journey: citizens are unsure how to prepare recyclable material, recyclers encounter mixed or unsafe waste without advance information, and collection centers need better visibility of incoming material.

I synthesized secondary research from ReciRed Bogotá (Universidad EAN, 2025) and a semi-structured field interview with Cecilia Gamboa, a recycler with ten years of experience. Her account of sorting bags by hand and encountering food, sanitary waste, and poorly packed glass made preparation and safety central to the design.
problem.question: How might we make preparing and handing over plastic simple for citizens, while giving recyclers the information and autonomy to collect it safely?

images.alt: Teach at the point of action. Knowing the recycling rules does not ensure correct separation. Give material-specific instructions immediately after the scan.
Make the handoff predictable. The interview highlighted contamination and missing information. Show material condition and risk notes before a recycler accepts.
Reduce the learning burden. Cecilia mainly used her phone for emergencies. A lightweight messaging flow was chosen as a hypothesis to test with recyclers.

paragraphs: I organized the citizen experience around four destinations: Home, Collections, Rewards, and Profile. Scanning starts from Home; classification and preparation lead into a collection request without becoming separate navigation sections.

The citizen selects an address and a proposed time within the next 24 hours. The recycler receives the request in Telegram and can accept, reject, or propose another time within that same window. A request remains pending until a recycler responds.

The wider service connects citizen → EcoGiro → recycler → collection center. Weight and material validation at the center support the operational roadmap; centralized payments belong to a later phase.

image.alt: EcoGiro information architecture divided into User and Agent. User includes medals, scanning and scheduled collection, recoveries and recovery detail, rewards, and profile with FAQ and data policy. Agent includes profile, accepted collections with recovery detail and collection scanning, and collections.

paragraphs: The documented structure prioritizes a single main action on Home: scan plastic. The material result then explains what to do before asking for quantity, address, and a collection time.

Scheduling keeps the material summary visible and separates sending a request from receiving confirmation. Empty, waiting, accepted, alternative-time, rejected, and collected states make the service status explicit.

items.title: One clear starting point
items.description: Keep the scan action prominent, with points and the next collection as supporting information.

items.title: Guidance before scheduling
items.description: Identify the material and explain cleaning, drying, flattening, and safe packing when applicable.

items.title: Confirmation is a distinct state
items.description: A sent request does not promise a pickup. Show the recycler response and let the citizen review an alternative time.

solution.subtitle: From a photo to a handoff
paragraphs: The EcoGiro MVP focused on one material stream and one understandable loop: photo → classification → preparation → request → recycler response → collection → traceability and points. The final screens show profile management, contextual help, Home, collection scheduling, and collection history.

features.title: Identify & prepare
paragraphs: AI-assisted classification considers categories such as PET, PP, PS, and ecoladrillo. The result explains the next preparation steps. Uncertain or incompatible results need a clear fallback rather than an unsupported identification.

features.title: Request & coordinate
features.benefit: People keep control of the handoff
paragraphs: Citizens choose their address and preferred time. Telegram gives recyclers material details and explicit response options. The 24-hour window is a product rule whose operational feasibility still needs a pilot.

features.title: Track & reward
paragraphs: Collection history and status keep the handoff visible. Eco-points are tied to completed, correctly prepared deliveries. Medals, challenges, and partner rewards are proposed incentives; commercial partnerships and environmental conversion formulas remain to be validated.

system.subtitle: A clear system for everyday actions
paragraphs: The visual direction supports short instructions, a visible primary action, and recognizable collection states. EcoGiro combines Poppins typography, Lucide React icons, the project palette, and an 8-point spacing scale.

foundations.title: Color
paragraphs: Green identifies primary actions; mint and cream separate content from the page. Coral supports destructive or error states, while light blue distinguishes active status. Labels and icons must carry the meaning alongside color.

foundations.title: Typography
paragraphs: Poppins is the typeface used for EcoGiro. Its rounded forms give the experience an approachable tone, while weight and size distinguish headings, preparation instructions, actions, and supporting information.
A clear hierarchy helps people scan material details and understand the next step without relying only on color or icons.

foundations.title: Iconography
paragraphs: EcoGiro uses Lucide React icons for navigation, scanning, collection, profile, and support. The original SVG components share a consistent line weight and use the project green. Text labels accompany icons in the interface.

foundations.title: Buttons
paragraphs: The specification calls for full-width primary actions, visible focus, pressed and disabled states, and touch targets of at least 44 px. Inline validation explains how to recover from an error. Contrast and accessibility remain requirements to verify, rather than audited outcomes.

components.title: Components
components.introduction: These components support EcoGiro’s collection, rewards, notifications, and location flows. The supplied specifications show their content, states, and dimensions.
components.conclusion: Reusable patterns keep information and actions recognizable across the experience, from choosing an address and time to reviewing a completed collection.

outcome.title: Outcome & Reflection
outcome.subtitle: Connect the service before scaling it
paragraphs: Over two months, the project brought research, experience structure, and interface design together into an MVP. My contribution connected research, the problem definition, user flows, the sitemap, contextual education, and the product narrative within a five-person team.

The business concept evolved toward collection centers as the priority B2B customer: an operated coordination and traceability service, with a proposed commission on material managed. Centralized payments are part of the future operating model. Pricing, center demand, and pickup economics remain hypotheses.

The supplied documents do not report product usability-test results, pilot performance, measured AI accuracy, or verified environmental gains. The next step is a small-area pilot with a collection center and a limited recycler group.

learnings.title: Safety starts before pickup
learnings.description: The field interview turned material preparation and risk information into core requirements. Better guidance should be evaluated through the quality of the material actually received.

learnings.title: Coordination requires autonomy
learnings.description: Citizen-selected scheduling and an explicit recycler response make both sides visible. Telegram adoption and the 24-hour window still need field validation.

learnings.title: A useful flow needs viable operations
learnings.description: Household convenience must be balanced with minimum pickup quantities, route density, center demand, and the cost of rewards.

metrics.title: Scan → request
metrics.description: Measure whether people understand the result and continue to a valid collection request.

metrics.title: Response → completed collection
metrics.description: Track recycler response time and the share of requests completed within the proposed window.

metrics.title: Quality & repeat use
metrics.description: Record validated kilograms, rejected or contaminated material, cost per kilogram, and a second collection within 30 days.

outcome.takeaway: Making recycling easier means designing the handoff as carefully as the interface.

0.title: Discovery
paragraphs: I structured the research questions and recycler interview guide, then synthesized the team’s field interview and secondary research. The strongest direction came from connecting everyday preparation mistakes with the effort and risks faced by recyclers.

1.title: UX / Structure
paragraphs: I mapped the citizen, recycler, and collection-center journeys and defined the MVP sitemap. The citizen flow moves from a photo to a request; Telegram gives the recycler information and a choice without requiring a dedicated EcoGiro app.

image.alt: EcoGiro scan result with environmental guidance, an estimated weight labeled as not measured, and the schedule collection action.
image.caption: UX / Structure ? From scan result to collection

2.title: UI Design
paragraphs: I translated the findings into contextual education and low-friction flows: short preparation instructions, one dominant scan action, visible request status, and eco-points after delivery. The UI direction uses familiar patterns to support the core journey across the two-month project.

image.alt: EcoGiro collection scheduling screen with a material summary, estimated weight, address, date, time slots, and an optional comment.
image.caption: UI Design ? Collection scheduling

3.title: Validation plan
paragraphs: The MVP connects the core journey from identification to handoff. The next validation stage is a pilot to test whether citizens trust the classification, recyclers can respond through Telegram, the collection window is realistic, and enough material can be collected to make each trip worthwhile.
